content:
The Supreme Court has clarified that revenue entries made without proper legal authority cannot establish or confer ownership rights over land. The ruling reinforces the distinction between revenue records and legal title, emphasising that mere mutation or revenue entries do not create ownership. The judgment highlights the importance of establishing property rights through valid legal documents and lawful title.

comment: A practical challenge is ensuring that buyers and lenders verify the underlying chain of title, not just the latest mutation entry. Errors in historical revenue records can complicate otherwise legitimate transactions.
